<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Saudi Arabian-led intervention in Yemen]]
**[[Houthis]] claim to have shot down a [[Royal Saudi Air Force]] [[F-15]] jet over [[Saada Governorate|Sa'da province]], [[Yemen]]. [https://sputniknews.com/middleeast/201803211062773665-houthi-rebels-saudi-arabia-jet/ (''Sputnik News'')]
*[[Syrian Civil War]]
**The [[Syria]]n government and rebel forces reach an agreement to allow 7,500 people to evacuate from rebel-held [[Harasta]], Eastern Ghouta. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2018/03/evacuation-deal-fighters-eastern-ghouta-town-reached-180321144929829.html (al-Jazeera)]
*[[Boko Haram insurgency]], [[Dapchi schoolgirls kidnapping]]
**[[Boko Haram]] releases most of the 110 [[Nigeria]]n schoolgirls it had kidnapped in February 2018, and warns against sending them back to school. [https://www.theglobeandmail.com/world/article-boko-haram-returns-most-schoolgirls-abducted-from-nigerias-dapchi/ (''The Globe and Mail'')]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[List of accidents and incidents involving helicopters|Accidents and incidents involving helicopters]]
**A [[Eurocopter EC120 Colibri|Eurocopter 120]] helicopter carrying five people crashes into the sea near Hardy Reef off the [[Whitsunday Islands]], [[Queensland]], [[Australia]]. Two people are killed. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2018/mar/21/whitsunday-helicopter-crash-deaths-great-barrier-reef-flight (''The Guardian'')]
*Aftermath of the [[2015 Shoreham Airshow crash]]
**The [[Crown Prosecution Service]] charges pilot Andrew Hill with 11 counts of manslaughter by gross negligence and one count of endangering an aircraft over an accident at [[Shoreham Airshow]] in [[England]]. [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2018/03/21/pilot-charged-manslaughter-shoreham-airshow-disaster-killed/ (''The Telegraph'')]
*[[Ballymun#2018 Metro Hotel Dublin fire|Metro Hotel Dublin fire]]
**A fire breaks out in the upper floors of a hotel and apartment block building in [[Ballymun]], [[Ireland]], near [[Dublin Airport]]. The fire affects the top seven floors of the building and two floors of apartments, without casualties. [https://www.rte.ie/news/ireland/2018/0321/949172-ballymun-fire/ (RTE)] [https://www.irishtimes.com/news/ireland/irish-news/fire-brigade-tackles-major-blaze-at-hotel-in-north-dublin-1.3435687 (''The Irish Times'')]
*[[History of autonomous cars]]
**Police release onboard video from an autonomous [[Uber]] car that fatally struck a pedestrian crossing the road in [[Tempe, Arizona]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-43497364 (BBC)]

;International relations
*[[Israel–Syria relations]]
**[[Israel]] admits for the first time that it [[Operation Outside the Box|carried out an airstrike]] on a suspected [[nuclear reactor]] in [[Deir ez-Zor Governorate]], [[Syria]], on 6 September 2007. The strike allegedly killed ten [[North Korea]]n workers. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-israel-syria-nuclear/israel-admits-bombing-suspected-syrian-nuclear-reactor-in-2007-warns-iran-idUSKBN1GX09K (Reuters)]
*[[Austria–Israel relations]]
**[[Austria]]n foreign minister [[Karin Kneissl]] recalls diplomat Jürgen-Michael Kleppich from [[Israel]] after he is photographed wearing a t-shirt with slogans linked to [[Nazism]]. [https://www.thelocal.at/20180321/austria-orders-diplomat-home-from-israel-after-posing-in-nazi-t-shirt (The Local)]
*[[Economy of the African Union]]
**The leaders of 44 [[African Union]] states sign an agreement in [[Kigali]], [[Rwanda]], to create the [[African Continental Free Trade Area]] (CFTA). [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-43489255 (BBC)]
*[[Poisoning of Sergei and Yulia Skripal]]
**[[Russia]] holds a briefing on the case for all foreign diplomats in [[Moscow]], where it accuses the [[United Kingdom]] of "withholding evidence." [https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2018/mar/21/russia-uk-evidence-sergei-skripal-case (The Guardian)]
*[[Poland in the European Union]]
**[[Poland|Polish]] Foreign Minister [[Jacek Czaputowicz]] accuses the [[European Union]] of "double standards" and of suffering  "a deficit of democracy". Poland and the [[European Commission]] are engaged in disputes over [[european migrant crisis|migrant quotas]] and proposed reform of Poland's judiciary. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2018/03/poland-accuses-eu-double-standards-180321161406615.html (al-Jazeera)]

;Law and crime
*[[Censorship in Singapore]]
**The [[Singapore]]an Parliament approves the Public Order and Safety (Special Powers) Act, which makes it a crime to take pictures and relay information during terror attacks. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/singapore/ban-photos-videos-messages-terrorist-posspa-10062836 (Channel News Asia)]
*[[Austin serial bombings]]
**Mark Anthony Conditt, the main suspect in the serial bombings, dies after detonating a bomb in his vehicle while being pursued by [[Austin Police Department|Austin police officers]]. The police chief warns residents that while they believe the bomber is deceased, he may have sent more packages before his death. [https://www.cnn.com/2018/03/21/us/austin-explosions/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Crime in the United Kingdom]]
**[[James Ibori]], a former governor of [[Delta State]], [[Nigeria]], launches a bid to overturn his guilty pleas on corruption charges in the [[United Kingdom|UK]] alleging police corruption. [http://www.africanews.com/2018/03/21/ex-nigerian-governor-ibori-appeals-against-fraud-conviction-accuses-british/ (Africa News)]
*[[Alleged Libyan influence in the 2007 French elections]]
**Former [[President of France]] [[Nicolas Sarkozy]] is preliminarily charged with illegal funding of his 2007 presidential campaign, passive corruption and receiving money from [[Libya|Libyan]] embezzlement. [https://www.voanews.com/a/french-official-says-sarkozy-charged-over-libyan-money-claims/4309395.html (Voice of America)]
*Aftermath of the [[2017 Parsons Green bombing]]
**''[[The Independent]]'' claims the [[Metropolitan Police]] misidentified material in convicted bomber Ahmad Hassan's possession as not related to [[ISIS]] when in fact it was produced by the group. The newspaper says it has submitted evidence to the [[Central Criminal Court (England and Wales)|Central Criminal Court]] that could affect Hassan's sentence. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/crime/parsons-green-attack-police-missed-isis-evidence-bombing-tube-a8267601.html (The Independent)]
*Police in [[the Philippines]] fatally shoot 13 suspected drug dealers in [[Bulacan]]. [http://www.france24.com/en/20180325-philippines-police-shoot-dead-duterte-quits-icc (France 24)]

;Politics and elections
*[[Politics of Myanmar]]
**[[President of Myanmar|Myanmar President]] [[Htin Kyaw]] resigns due to ill health. Vice-President [[Myint Swe (general)|Myint Swe]], a former general, will become acting president until a new president is chosen. [https://www.cnn.com/2018/03/21/asia/myanmar-president-htin-kyaw-resigns-intl/index.html (CNN)] [https://www.usnews.com/news/world/articles/2018-03-21/myanmars-president-resigns-to-take-rest-from-duties (''U.S. News & World Report'')] [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-43482191 (BBC)]
* Jackfruit becomes official state fruit of [[Kerala]].
*[[2017–18 Spanish constitutional crisis]]
**[[Catalonia|Catalan]] activist [[Jordi Sànchez i Picanyol]], imprisoned accused of sedition, drops his bid to lead the Catalan government. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-43483946 (BBC)]
**[[Jordi Turull|Jordi Turull i Negre]], ex-member of the dismissed regional government, who was imprisoned amid sedition and under investigation due to his connection in a corruption scandal involving [[Convergència i Unió|CiU]], is named candidate by the [[President of the Parliament of Catalonia|President of Catalan Parliament]] in an investiture for Thursday, March 22. [http://www.elmundo.es/cataluna/2018/03/21/5ab2997aca4741920d8b45e9.html (''El Mundo'')]
*[[Resignation of Pedro Pablo Kuczynski]]
**[[President of Peru|Peruvian President]] [[Pedro Pablo Kuczynski]] resigns amid a [[vote buying]] scandal. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-43492421 (BBC)]
*[[Antiguan general election, 2018]]
**Voters in [[Antigua and Barbuda]] go to the polls, with [[Barbuda]]n residents having to travel to [[Antigua]] in order to participate. [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2018/03/21/barbudans-forced-travel-antigua-vote-islanders-fear-future-land/ (The Telegraph)]
*[[Politics of Kosovo]]
**In [[Kosovo]], opposition lawmakers set off tear gas to prevent the ratification of a border treaty with neighboring [[Montenegro]]. [https://www.cnn.com/2018/03/21/europe/kosovo-parliament-tear-gas-intl/index.html (CNN)]

;Science and technology 
*[[Discoveries of exoplanets]]
**Fifteen new [[exoplanet]]s are discovered. Three of them, larger than [[Earth]], are also discovered around the dwarf star K2-155. Furthermore, a 3D climate simulation was created to find out if [[K2-155d]] has water. [https://www.healththoroughfare.com/news/15-new-alien-worlds-discovered-recently/6135 (''Health Thoroughfare'')] [https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2018/03/180312085057.htm (ScienceDaily)]
*[[2018 in spaceflight]]
**Three people (two [[United States|American]], one [[Russia|Russian]]) launch successfully from the [[Baikonur Cosmodrome]] aboard [[Soyuz MS-08]] to the [[International Space Station]] as part of [[Expedition 55]]. [https://www.nasa.gov/press-release/two-nasa-astronauts-among-crew-heading-to-international-space-station (NASA)]
